title: Binary Search & Parametric Search (Depth Pass)
relevance: High (second wave of CF-style BS-on-answer / parametric checks beyond the classic OA templates)
company_notes: Threshold scheduling: minimum days so every monster/task is cleared by some worker with cooldown/endurance (Final Boss / Monster Killing family). Facility radius: smallest Wi-Fi/tower radius covering all clients (Cellular Network clone, common in OA). Budgeted median: raise salaries so the median is at least X without exceeding budget S (Salary Changing). Hidden k-th: k-th product / table entry / pair sum without materializing O(n^2) pairs — classic phone-screen follow-up to plain binary search.

phases.goal: Spot a hidden monotone decision problem where contest text never says binary search but a threshold X is checkable near-linearly.

must_hit.point: After the standard ladder (Koko / ship packages / Hamburgers / min-max partition), problems hide a monotonic decision: guess a threshold X (time, capacity, strength, median, party size), then answer YES/NO with greedy, two pointers, prefix/diff arrays, or BFS.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names a threshold X and a yes/no check built from greedy, two pointers, prefix/diff, or BFS rather than a named binary-search template.

must_hit.point: Recognize it when the answer range is huge (10^9–10^18) but a fixed X can be validated in near-linear time, and feasibility is monotone in X.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites a 10^9–10^18-scale answer range plus cheap near-linear validation and monotonicity in X.

must_hit.point: OA/interview skins include threshold scheduling (Final Boss / Monster Killing), facility radius (Cellular Network), budgeted median (Salary Changing), and hidden k-th without materializing O(n^2) pairs.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps the prompt to one of those four skins: scheduling days, tower radius, budgeted median, or implicit k-th.

probes: What tells you this is a hidden parametric / BS-on-answer problem rather than a classic OA Koko-style template?
If the answer range is huge but checking a fixed X is near-linear and monotone, what do you reach for?

hints.1: Ask whether the statement hides a threshold with a yes/no check instead of announcing binary search.
hints.2: Look for a huge answer range plus a near-linear monotone feasibility check in X.
hints.3: Say: guess X (time/capacity/strength/median/party size), validate with greedy/two pointers/prefix-diff/BFS; cue is 10^9–10^18 range with monotone near-linear check.

phases.goal: Formulate the monotone check and choose the right predicate engine: rewrite, coverage greedy, cost-of-k resort, k-th count, graph threshold, or diff-array.

must_hit.point: Rewrite the check until it is obviously monotone: “can we achieve median/height/time ≥ X?” beats inventing a direct formula.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States a can-we-achieve ≥ X style predicate and refuses a closed-form first attempt.

must_hit.point: Coverage checks (Cellular / Wooden Toy / Office Keys): sort both sides, then two-pointer or “next uncovered” greedy; if the greedy fails, mid is impossible.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sorts both sides and runs two-pointer or next-uncovered greedy, treating greedy failure as mid impossible.

must_hit.point: Cost-depends-on-k (Sagheer): when taking k items changes each item’s cost, re-sort for that k inside the check — do not reuse one global order.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Recomputes costs a_i + i·k for the guessed k, re-sorts, and prefix-sums inside the check.

must_hit.point: k-th in an implicit sorted list (multiplication table / pair products): BS the value v, count how many entries ≤ v in O(n) or O(n log).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Binary-searches the value and counts ≤ v without building the full list.

must_hit.point: Parametric + graph (Jumping Takahashi): edges appear as S grows; BS S and only rebuild/BFS the threshold graph — do not Dijkstra over all S.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Binary-searches strength S, rebuilds edges at the threshold, and BFS/reachability-checks rather than Dijkstra over all S.

probes: How do you rewrite the ask into a monotone feasibility check?
For coverage or cost-depends-on-k, what do you do inside the mid check?
For an implicit k-th or a parametric graph, what do you search and what do you rebuild?

hints.1: Start from “can we achieve ≥ X?” before hunting a formula.
hints.2: Coverage → sort both sides + greedy/two pointers; Sagheer → re-sort costs for that k; k-th → count ≤ v; graph → BS S + rebuild/BFS.
hints.3: Say: monotone rewrite; coverage greedy fails ⇒ mid impossible; re-sort for k; BS v and count ≤ v; BS S and BFS the threshold graph, not Dijkstra over all S.

phases.goal: Show safe mid arithmetic, i64 overflow hygiene, fixed-iteration float BS, and O(1)-amortized updates inside the check.

must_hit.point: Prefer mid = lo + (hi-lo)/2; damage × turns, n·mid, and ∑ mid/i all need i64.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses mid = lo + (hi-lo)/2 and i64 for those product/sum patterns.

must_hit.point: Float / continuous answers: run a fixed 80–100 iterations (Meeting Place); never while (hi-lo > 1e-9) under tight TL.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses a fixed 80–100 iteration loop and rejects an EPS-style while (hi-lo > 1e-9).

must_hit.point: Diff-array / sliding window inside check (Present): “add +1 on [i,i+w)” is O(1) amortized per index after a difference array, so total check stays O(n).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Places difference marks for window adds and rebuilds so each index is amortized O(1) and the check is O(n).

must_hit.point: Sagheer-style cost rewrite: cost of taking k items becomes a_i + i·k; sort and prefix-sum inside the check for that k.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rebuilds a_i + i·k, sorts, and prefix-sums per mid/k inside the predicate.

probes: What mid formula and integer type do you use when products like damage × turns or ∑ mid/i appear?
How do you binary-search a continuous answer without EPS TLE?
How does a difference array keep a watering / sliding-window check O(n)?

hints.1: Think safe mid, wide integers, fixed float iterations, and amortized updates in the predicate.
hints.2: mid = lo + (hi-lo)/2 with i64; floats use 80–100 fixed iters; window adds go through a diff array.
hints.3: Spell: mid = lo+(hi-lo)/2; i64 on damage×turns / n·mid / ∑ mid/i; 80–100 iters not while (hi-lo > 1e-9); +1 on [i,i+w) via diff so check stays O(n).

phases.goal: Keep each mid check near-linear (or O(n)/O(n log) counts) and refuse materializing huge implicit lists or all-S graph searches.

must_hit.point: A fixed X is validated in near-linear time while the answer range stays huge (10^9–10^18), so search cost is log of the range times one check.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates near-linear per-mid validation from logarithmic guesses over a 10^9–10^18 answer range.

must_hit.point: For k-th in an implicit list, count entries ≤ v in O(n) or O(n log) rather than materializing O(n^2) pairs.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Quotes O(n) or O(n log) counting per mid and refuses building the full pair/table list.

must_hit.point: Present-style diff-array check stays O(n) because each window add is O(1) amortized per index after the difference array.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Charges the check as O(n) via amortized O(1) difference updates per index.

probes: What is the per-mid cost you expect when the answer range is 10^9–10^18?
How do you count for an implicit k-th without O(n^2) materialization?
Why does a difference-array watering check stay O(n)?

hints.1: Separate log guesses from the cost of one feasibility check.
hints.2: Near-linear (or O(n)/O(n log) count) per mid; never build O(n^2) pairs; diff keeps watering O(n).
hints.3: Say: log over 10^9–10^18 × near-linear check; count ≤ v in O(n) or O(n log); Present check O(n) via amortized O(1) diff updates.

phases.goal: Catch global-order reuse, overflow, EPS float loops, Dijkstra-over-S, and formula-first mistakes the depth ladder punishes.

must_hit.point: When taking k items changes each item’s cost, do not reuse one global order — re-sort for that k inside the check.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Catches sorting once globally and forces a_i + i·k re-sort per guessed k.

must_hit.point: Integer overflow on damage × turns, n·mid, and ∑ mid/i — use i64 and mid = lo + (hi-lo)/2.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names those overflow sites and switches to i64 with safe mid.

must_hit.point: Never while (hi-lo > 1e-9) under tight TL for continuous answers; use fixed 80–100 iterations.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects the EPS while-loop and states a fixed 80–100 iteration float BS.

must_hit.point: On parametric graphs, do not Dijkstra over all S — BS S and only rebuild/BFS the threshold graph.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Redirects from Dijkstra-over-S to binary search on S plus rebuild/BFS.

must_hit.point: Inventing a direct formula instead of rewriting to “can we achieve median/height/time ≥ X?” misses the monotone check.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Abandons a closed form and restates a monotone ≥ X feasibility predicate.

probes: What goes wrong if Sagheer-style costs are sorted only once globally?
Which overflow and float-loop mistakes show up in Final Boss / Meeting Place style checks?
Why is Dijkstra over all S the wrong move on Jumping Takahashi-style problems?

hints.1: Check order reuse, integer width, float termination, and graph search choice.
hints.2: Re-sort per k; i64 + safe mid; fixed 80–100 iters; BS+BFS not Dijkstra-over-S.
hints.3: Also: rewrite to a monotone ≥ X check instead of inventing a direct formula.

tradeoffs.topic: Monotone feasibility rewrite vs inventing a direct formula
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Rewrite the check until it is obviously monotone: “can we achieve median/height/time ≥ X?” beats inventing a direct formula.

tradeoffs.topic: Re-sort costs for guessed k vs one global sort order
tradeoffs.strong_answer: When taking k items changes each item’s cost (Sagheer: a_i + i·k), re-sort for that k inside the check and prefix-sum — do not reuse one global order.
For continuous answers (Meeting Place), run a fixed 80–100 iterations; never while (hi-lo > 1e-9) under tight TL.

tradeoffs.topic: BS value + count ≤ v vs materializing O(n^2) pairs
tradeoffs.strong_answer: For k-th in an implicit sorted list (multiplication table / pair products), BS the value v and count how many entries ≤ v in O(n) or O(n log) instead of materializing O(n^2) pairs.

tradeoffs.topic: BS S + rebuild/BFS threshold graph vs Dijkstra over all S
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Edges appear as S grows (Jumping Takahashi); BS S and only rebuild/BFS the threshold graph — do not Dijkstra over all S.

tradeoffs.topic: Difference-array window adds vs naive per-mid resim of watering
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Inside Present-style checks, “add +1 on [i,i+w)” is O(1) amortized per index after a difference array, so the total check stays O(n).

gotchas.trap: Reusing one global sort order when item costs depend on the guessed k.
gotchas.correction: Re-sort for that k inside the check (cost becomes a_i + i·k); prefix-sum after sorting.

gotchas.trap: Integer overflow on damage × turns, n·mid, or ∑ mid/i, or mid = (lo+hi)/2 overflow risk.
gotchas.correction: Use i64 for those products/sums and prefer mid = lo + (hi-lo)/2.
Run a fixed 80–100 iterations (Meeting Place), not an EPS while-loop.

gotchas.trap: Dijkstra over all S when edges appear as strength S grows.
gotchas.correction: BS S and only rebuild/BFS the threshold graph (Jumping Takahashi).

gotchas.trap: Coverage greedy succeeds/fails ignored as the feasibility oracle.
gotchas.correction: Sort both sides, then two-pointer or “next uncovered” greedy; if the greedy fails, mid is impossible.

gotchas.trap: Inventing a direct formula instead of a monotone check.
gotchas.correction: Rewrite until the ask is “can we achieve median/height/time ≥ X?” with a yes/no predicate.

gotchas.trap: Materializing all pairs/table entries to find a k-th value.
gotchas.correction: BS the value v and count how many entries ≤ v in O(n) or O(n log).
